findings.passage: We go to great lengths to secure our financial records, health records, and homes. During the COVID-19 pandemic, many establishments required a COVID-19 vaccine to enter along with a photo ID for proof of identity. Banks require a photo ID to open an account or secure a loan to protect against fraud. The same should be done for our elections. Our goal should be ZERO fraud in our elections, and any amount of voter fraud is unacceptable.
findings.note: Op-ed on his official Assembly site, written as chair of the Assembly elections committee, arguing for photo ID to vote.

findings.passage: Wisconsin law currently requires a photo ID to vote. However, enshrining voter ID requirements in the state constitution will prevent a minority viewpoint from overruling the will of the voters. This will now go before the voters to decide whether to amend the state's constitution. I am proud to support this measure.
findings.note: Same op-ed: says he supports putting the existing photo ID requirement into the state constitution (April 2025 ballot question).

findings.passage: If there was one action we could have taken simultaneously, it would be to mandate voter IDs to also confirm citizenship. However, Wisconsin's voter ID law has been largely effective in ensuring election integrity and boosting public confidence in our elections.
findings.note: Written testimony to a Kansas House elections committee on a Kansas voter ID constitutional amendment (HCR 5021). He says a citizenship check tied to voter ID would have been the one added step, and calls the current Wisconsin law effective.
subjects: proof of citizenship tied to voter ID

findings.passage: Wisconsin's voter ID law was enacted in 2014 and has not resulted in voter suppression. On the contrary, voter participation has increased since its implementation.
findings.note: Same Kansas testimony: says Wisconsin's ID law has not suppressed voting.

findings.passage: “I am honored and excited to lead this important committee and continue working to improve the integrity of our election system,” said Representative Maxey, “Wisconsin voters deserve secure and transparent elections, and I remain committed to ensuring their voices are protected. I look forward to advancing legislation that upholds these principles.”
findings.note: Official release on his naming as elections committee chair; general statement on election integrity, no specific ID or citizenship rule named.
